subproblem.title: Lebesgue points for Hⁿ⌞S with the ρⁿ normalization under an upper density bound (Simon Ch. 1, 3.17; parent (P3))
subproblem.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, S ⊆ ℝ^N Hⁿ-null-measurable with Hⁿ(S) < ∞, w : ℝ^N → ℝ integrable on S with respect to Hⁿ, and C ∈ ℝ such that Hⁿ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Cρⁿ) for all x ∈ S and ρ > 0. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S: lim_{ρ↓0} ρ^{-n}∫_{S ∩ B_ρ(x)} |w(z) − w(x)| dHⁿ(z) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (S : Set (Rn N)) (w : Rn N → ℝ) (C : ℝ), NullMeasurableSet S μHE[n] → μHE[n] S < ∞ → IntegrableOn w S μHE[n] → (∀ x ∈ S, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → μHE[n] (S ∩ Metric.closedBall x ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * ρ ^ n)) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Rn N)), x ∈ S → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ ↦ (ρ ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ z in S ∩ Metric.ball x ρ, |w z - w x| ∂μHE[n]) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof Step 3, (P3): the Lebesgue-Besicovitch differentiation theorem (Simon Ch. 1, Corollary 3.17, with the Symmetric Vitali property of Radon measures on ℝ^N from Besicovitch's covering lemma 3.12) for the finite Radon measure λ₀ = Hⁿ⌞S, converted to the ρⁿ normalization through the upper bound λ₀(B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ Cρⁿ. Mathlib: VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub for Besicovitch.vitaliFamily, composed with Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt. (No Borel version of w is needed: the Mathlib theorem applies to every locally integrable function.) All lemmas cited are available after `import GMT.Ch03.Submission`.

1. λ₀ := Hⁿ⌞S (Mathlib μHE[n].restrict S) is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^N, since λ₀(ℝ^N) = Hⁿ(S) < ∞; in the formalization, record the instance IsFiniteMeasure λ₀ explicitly (from Hⁿ(S) < ∞), which provides the SFinite and IsLocallyFiniteMeasure instances required below. By hypothesis w is λ₀-integrable, hence locally integrable with respect to λ₀.

2. ℝ^N, a finite-dimensional real normed space, has the Besicovitch covering property, so Besicovitch.vitaliFamily λ₀ is a Vitali family for λ₀. The Lebesgue differentiation theorem along this family (VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub) gives: for λ₀-a.e. x, the averages ⨍_E |w(z) − w(x)| dλ₀(z) tend to 0 as E shrinks to x along (Besicovitch.vitaliFamily λ₀).filterAt x. By Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt, ρ ↦ B̄_ρ(x) tends to this filter as ρ ↓ 0. Hence for λ₀-a.e. x: a(ρ) := ⨍_{B̄_ρ(x)} |w(z) − w(x)| dλ₀(z) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0, where ⨍_E h dλ₀ = λ₀(E)^{-1}∫_E h dλ₀ (and = 0 when λ₀(E) = 0). (Simon Ch. 1, 3.17.)

3. Since S is Hⁿ-null-measurable, 'for λ₀-a.e. x' is equivalent to 'for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S' (Mathlib ae_restrict_iff'₀). Fix x ∈ S with a(ρ) → 0 and put C⁺ := max(C, 0). By hypothesis, λ₀(B̄_ρ(x)) = Hⁿ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ C⁺ρⁿ for every ρ > 0.

4. Fix ρ > 0 and let h(z) := |w(z) − w(x)| ≥ 0. h is λ₀-integrable (w is, and constants are because λ₀ is finite). Then ∫_{S ∩ B_ρ(x)} h dHⁿ = ∫_{B_ρ(x)} h dλ₀ ≤ ∫_{B̄_ρ(x)} h dλ₀ (Measure.restrict_restrict, setIntegral_mono_set). If λ₀(B̄_ρ(x)) = 0, the last integral is 0. Otherwise it equals λ₀(B̄_ρ(x))·a(ρ) ≤ C⁺ρⁿ·a(ρ), as a(ρ) ≥ 0. In all cases 0 ≤ ρ^{-n}∫_{S ∩ B_ρ(x)} |w(z) − w(x)| dHⁿ(z) ≤ C⁺a(ρ).

5. As ρ ↓ 0, C⁺a(ρ) → 0; by the squeeze principle ρ^{-n}∫_{S ∩ B_ρ(x)} |w(z) − w(x)| dHⁿ(z) → 0. By step 3 this holds for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S. (The argument is unchanged for n = 0, where S is finite.) ∎
proof_key_steps: λ₀ = Hⁿ⌞S is a finite Borel measure (IsFiniteMeasure instance) and w ∈ L¹(λ₀).
Lebesgue-Besicovitch differentiation (VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub + Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt): ⨍_{B̄_ρ(x)} |w − w(x)| dλ₀ → 0 for λ₀-a.e. x.
λ₀-a.e. x ⇔ Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S (S null-measurable).

audit.reason: The finite restricted measure satisfies the differentiation theorem's requirements. Null-measurability transfers its almost-everywhere conclusion to the stated ambient implication. The density bound gives the normalized squeeze estimate, with zero-mass balls and possibly negative C handled explicitly.
